# Introduction

In this assignment we build two families of models on auto insurance customer data: (1) binary
logistic regression models predicting `TARGET_FLAG`, whether a customer will crash their car, and
(2) multiple linear regression models predicting `TARGET_AMT`, the cost of the crash given that
one occurs.

# Data Exploration

```{r load-data}
#| label: load-data

train = read_csv("data/insurance-training-data.csv")
evaluation = read_csv("data/insurance-evaluation-data.csv")

train = train %>% select(-INDEX)
```

## Size and Structure

Data contains 8161 observations, 23 predictors, and 2 target variables.
Variables such as `INCOME` and `BLUEBOOK` currently coded as characters due to leading $. These will need to be transformed to numeric variables for use in models.

```{r data-structure}
#| label: data-structure

tibble(
  Variable = names(train),
  Type     = map_chr(train, ~ class(.x)[1]),
  Example  = map_chr(train, ~ paste(head(.x, 3), collapse = ", "))
) |>
  kable()

dim(train)
```

## Summary Statistics

```{r summary-stats}
#| label: summary-stats

describe(train) |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  rownames_to_column("Variable") |>
  select(Variable, mean, sd, median, se) |>
  kable(digits = 2)
```

## Cleaning Currency and Categorical Fields

```{r clean-fields}
#| label: clean-fields

train = train |>
  mutate(across(c(INCOME, HOME_VAL, BLUEBOOK, OLDCLAIM), 
         ~ as.numeric(str_replace_all(.x, "[^0-9.]", ""))),
         across(!where(is.numeric), as.factor))
```

## Correlation with Targets

```{r correlation}
#| label: fig-correlation

cor_matrix <- train |>
  select(where(is.numeric)) |>
  cor(use = "pairwise.complete.obs")

# Then we can plot the corr plot
corrplot(cor_matrix,
         method = "color",
         type = "lower",
         order = "hclust",
         addCoef.col = "black",
         number.cex = 0.6,

         tl.srt = 45,
         diag = FALSE)
```

## Missing Data

```{r missing-data}
#| label: missing-data

missing_props = train_long_num |>
  group_by(variable) |>
  summarise(
    proportion_missing = mean(is.na(value)),
    .groups = "drop") |>
  rbind(train_long_chr |>
          group_by(variable) |>
          summarise(proportion_missing = mean(is.na(value)), .groups = "drop"))

ggplot(missing_props, aes(x = reorder(variable, proportion_missing),
                          y = proportion_missing)) +
  geom_col(fill = "#3a86d4") +
  coord_flip() +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Proportion missing", title = "Missing Data by Variable") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12)
```


## Feature Transformations

_Describe any bucketing, log/sqrt/Box-Cox transforms, or derived variables and the rationale for each._

```{r transformations}
#| label: transformations

sapply(
  train_imputed |> dplyr::select(where(is.numeric)),
  \(x) BoxCoxTrans(x)$lambda
)

num_data <- train_imputed |>
  dplyr::select(where(is.numeric), -TARGET_FLAG, -TARGET_AMT)

# how much to add to each column so its smallest value becomes 1
shift_amt <- sapply(num_data, \(x) {
  m <- min(x, na.rm = TRUE)
  if (m <= 0) 1 - m else 0
})

# see which columns get shifted
shift_amt[shift_amt > 0]   

# helper that adds the stored shift to each column
apply_shift <- function(df, shifts) {
  for (col in names(shifts)) df[[col]] <- df[[col]] + shifts[[col]]
  df
}

# Shift first, then Box-Cox / center / scale
num_shifted <- apply_shift(num_data, shift_amt)

pp <- preProcess(num_shifted, method = c("BoxCox", "center", "scale"))
lambdas <- sapply(pp$bc, \(x) x$lambda)
lambdas

train_pp <- predict(pp, num_shifted)

# Evaluation data: same shift, same pp
eval_shifted <- apply_shift(
  eval_imputed |> dplyr::select(all_of(names(num_data))),
  shift_amt
)
eval_pp <- predict(pp, eval_shifted)

train_pp |>
  pivot_longer(
  cols = where(is.numeric),   
  names_to = "variable",      
  values_to = "value") |>
  ggplot(aes(x = value)) +
  geom_density(bins = 20, fill = "#3a86d4", colour = "white") +
  facet_wrap(~ variable, scales = "free") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Count", title = "Variable Distributions") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 9.6)
```
